title: DSL Conformance Max
purpose: DSL surface-coverage fixture. A corpus-wide measurement (2026-07-29) found 7 schema features exercised by ZERO of the 29 corpus models and 6 more carried by a single model -- including `aggregates`/`autoPanels`/`guidePages`, which lived only in WmsOffice and its byte-identical clone. This model exists to close those gaps so a schema or compiler change that breaks them fails the corpus-parse gate instead of shipping unnoticed.
businessStory: Deliberately thin: a widget order with owned lines, a catalog to pick SKUs from, and a nightly sweep. The domain is a vehicle for the DSL surface, not the point. Do NOT use this as an authoring example -- read `simple-contact-intake` or `medium-expense-approval` for that.
features: step: scheduleEvent -- both delivery modes (delaySeconds: 0 publishes inline, delaySeconds: 3600 defers through npdev_scheduled_event)
step: invariantCheck, createConcept, emitEvent, capabilityCall, return
webhooks (inbound, HMAC-SHA256, POST /api/hooks/{source}) + step: awaitEvent resumed by it
walkthrough: This fixture is validated AND generated (docs/CLOSEOUT_PLAN.md G2): `scripts/quality/validate-corpus.py` parses it on every knowledge-gate run, and `scripts/quality/check-dsl-conformance-generates.py` generates it for real and asserts its rare features survive into the compiled output on every PR gate run.
To check it by hand: gradlew :NPDevContract:dsl:validateModel -PmodelPath=<this dir>/model.json -PreportOut=<out>.json
When you add a DSL feature, add it HERE too -- that is what keeps the corpus honest.
